slides.title:
Repair the fault,
then prove the uptime
slides.subtitle:
Synthetic community microgrid / one critical-load bus
30-day availability: 98.96%; planning target: 99.50%.
slides.notes: Dark command-style opener contrasts with light evidence pages and dark decision strips. Availability means bus output within the assumed operating specification, not energy adequacy, household uptime, or electrical safety certification. All events, costs, targets, and proposed roles are invented.

slides.title: Reserve USD 2,400; release no work yet
slides.subtitle: Synthetic decision: connector replacement is conditional, not authorized
bullets: Prefer connector replacement only if qualified diagnosis confirms the suspected fault.
Facilities lead must verify backup continuity, the approved work permit, and the replacement part.
Use qualified electrical personnel and site procedures; this deck is not a repair instruction or safety certification.
slides.summary_callout: Budget reservation is not permission to isolate, repair, or re-energize the microgrid.
slides.notes: Decision precedes exhibits because the team needs a clear conditional request before examining the event evidence. USD 2,400 is a planning estimate, not a vendor quote. This is not guidance for an actual energized system.

slides.title: One suspected fault tags 60% of downtime
slides.subtitle: Synthetic, non-overlapping events on the same 720-hour bus window

options.catAxisTitle: Event tag; suspected cause is not confirmed

slides.caption: SYN-O1. Availability = (720 - 7.5) / 720 = 98.9583%, rounded to 98.96%. The connector tag accounts for 4.5/7.5 = 60%; attribution is a hypothesis, not proven causality.
slides.notes: Four events are mutually exclusive and counted once. Planned downtime is included in both the actual metric and the target definition. No exclusions for maintenance or customer count weighting.

slides.title: Cost alone cannot select the repair
slides.subtitle: Synthetic planning estimates; no option has demonstrated reliability gain

rows: May leave damaged hardware in service
Hold unless module damage is confirmed
table.caption: SYN-O2. Estimates include parts and labor, exclude taxes and contingency. Outage is the assumed bus interruption, not total crew time. No lead time, quote, failure probability, or safety approval is supplied.

slides.notes: These are alternative options, not additive project costs. The budget request matches the connector option. A lower cost is not evidence of adequate protection; all work requires qualified diagnosis and local procedures.

slides.title: Three gates stand between budget and service
slides.subtitle: Synthetic process register; owners are proposed roles, not named staff

milestones.label: BEFORE / facilities
milestones.title: Confirm readiness
milestones.body: Qualified diagnosis, approved permit, correct part, and verified critical-load backup. Stop if any is missing.

milestones.label: WORK / qualified crew
milestones.title: Execute site procedure
milestones.body: Only authorized personnel perform isolation and repair under approved local procedures. No live-work method is given here.

milestones.label: AFTER / commissioning
milestones.title: Verify before release
milestones.body: Document site-required tests and authorized sign-off before service release; preserve event logs for follow-up.

slides.caption: SYN-O2. Readiness and commissioning are gates, not a how-to guide. A passed functional check does not certify long-term uptime or eliminate electrical risk.
slides.notes: Editable sequential process uses supported timeline objects rather than raster Mermaid. No calendar dates or unsupported work completion claims. Qualified personnel own technical procedures and safety approval.

slides.title: Even a perfect repair misses this target
slides.subtitle: Synthetic same-window counterfactual, not a prediction of the next month

right.title: Optimistic substitution
bullets: Remove all 4.5 connector-tagged hours; add 1.5 repair hours.
Still 0.9 hours over allowance; other faults remain.

slides.verdict: Do not promise 99.50% uptime from the connector replacement alone.
slides.notes: The hypothetical applies to the same 720-hour denominator, holds the other 3.0 hours unchanged, assumes perfect prevention of the suspected event, and inserts the proposed 1.5-hour bus outage. It is deliberately optimistic and cannot predict recurrence or the next window.

slides.title: Close the work order, keep the uptime gate
slides.subtitle: Synthetic acceptance register: functional release and reliability are separate

quadrants.title: Commissioning
quadrants.body: Document site tests; require authorized sign-off. Without sign-off, no service release.

quadrants.title: Operations
quadrants.body: Log all events and missing-data intervals in the next full 720 h, including planned downtime.

quadrants.title: Maintenance
quadrants.body: Require qualified reassessment for any connector-tagged recurrence; keep it in aggregate uptime.

quadrants.title: Facilities
quadrants.body: Full 720 h coverage: target downtime <=3.6 h. Incomplete coverage: uptime unverified.

slides.summary_callout: Conditional repair readiness only; no actual repair, safety approval, or uptime achievement is asserted.
sources: SYN-O1/O2 | all facts, estimates, and gates invented
slides.notes: SYN-O1 denotes the invented availability ledger and target. SYN-O2 denotes invented planning estimates, roles, and gates. Neither is an external citation. No external assets or source licensing issues. A future target check is an acceptance criterion, not an achieved result.
